explain: Real-time endpoints keep provisioned instances warm behind an HTTPS endpoint, giving consistent low-latency predictions. Batch, serverless, and asynchronous options all add delay unsuited to sub-second fraud scoring.
options: Deploy a SageMaker real-time endpoint with provisioned instances for low-latency inference
Run a SageMaker batch transform job that scores accumulated transactions once every hour
Deploy a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint that cold-starts on every sporadic request
Deploy an asynchronous endpoint that queues each payment and returns results via Amazon S3
q: A payment company needs fraud scores in under 100 ms for each transaction, 24/7. Which deployment should it use?

explain: Serverless Inference scales to zero and bills per invocation, which fits sporadic traffic with tolerant latency. A provisioned real-time endpoint would sit idle and cost money most of the day.
options: Keep a real-time endpoint on ml.m5.xlarge instances running continuously through idle periods
Deploy a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint that scales to zero and bills per invocation
Launch a batch transform job on a fixed schedule that precomputes predictions for every user
Deploy an asynchronous endpoint with large instances and provisioned concurrency always enabled
q: A startup gets a few hundred unpredictable prediction requests per day and tolerates cold starts. What is the most cost-effective option?

explain: Asynchronous inference queues requests and handles long processing times up to an hour, notifying via SNS on completion. Real-time endpoints time out after 60 seconds and batch transform is not request-driven.
options: A real-time endpoint with autoscaling that returns every prediction synchronously within seconds
A batch transform job that runs nightly over all stored images regardless of arrival patterns
An asynchronous inference endpoint that queues each image and notifies completion via SNS
A multi-model endpoint that loads every model variant into memory for instant synchronous use
q: An app receives large images at irregular times and each inference takes up to 5 minutes. Which option fits best?

explain: Batch transform is designed for large offline datasets stored in S3, running without a persistent endpoint. Paying for an always-on endpoint to score a nightly backlog wastes money.
options: A real-time endpoint with provisioned instances kept running all night for interactive queries
A Serverless Inference endpoint invoked millions of times in a tight loop with maximum concurrency until the backlog ends
An asynchronous endpoint with one-by-one invocations and SNS notifications for every single row
A SageMaker batch transform job that scores the full S3 dataset nightly with no persistent endpoint
q: A retailer scores millions of stored customer rows once per night with no latency requirement. Which option should it choose?

explain: Multi-model endpoints host many models on shared containers and load them on demand, which is ideal for hundreds of rarely used variants. Separate real-time endpoints would multiply idle costs.
options: A multi-model endpoint that hosts all variants on shared containers and loads them on demand
One dedicated real-time endpoint per variant with provisioned instances and reserved capacity running continuously
A nightly batch transform job that precomputes predictions for every variant and every input
A Serverless Inference endpoint per variant with maximum memory configured for peak bursts
q: A company serves hundreds of small per-client model variants, each invoked rarely. How can it minimize cost?

explain: SageMaker Pipelines has a dedicated TrainingStep that launches training jobs inside the pipeline. Processing steps run preprocessing scripts, while evaluation and registration serve other stages.
options: A ProcessingStep that runs a preprocessing script on the training data before model fitting
A TrainingStep that launches a managed SageMaker training job as part of the pipeline flow
A QualityCheckStep that computes metrics on a held-out test set after the model is trained
A RegisterModel step that adds the trained artifact to the Model Registry with its metadata
q: Which SageMaker Pipelines step actually launches a model training job inside the pipeline?

explain: The Model Registry versions models and tracks approval status such as PendingManualApproval and Approved. Pipeline steps execute work, but gating production deployment is the registry's approval workflow.
options: A SageMaker training job that retrains the model nightly and overwrites the previous artifact
A ConditionStep that recomputes accuracy metrics on each new candidate model build
The Model Registry approval workflow that gates deployment until a reviewer marks it Approved
An EventBridge rule that automatically restarts failed pipeline executions with doubled capacity
q: A bank requires a human reviewer to approve each model version before production. Which feature enforces this gate?

explain: SageMaker Projects provide templates that provision CodePipeline and CodeBuild resources for build, test, and deploy stages. Pipelines alone orchestrate ML steps but do not provision CI/CD infrastructure.
options: A SageMaker Pipeline defined in the notebook that retrains the model on a fixed weekly schedule with manual approvals
A Step Functions workflow that chains Lambda functions to copy artifacts between S3 buckets
An EventBridge rule that triggers retraining whenever new labeled data lands in the S3 prefix
A SageMaker Project template that provisions CodePipeline and CodeBuild stages for the ML workflow
q: A team wants versioned CI/CD with build, test, and deploy stages for its ML code. Which service provides ready-made templates?

explain: Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows with retries, branching, and error handling across services. EventBridge routes events, Lambda runs single functions, and MWAA schedules Airflow DAGs.
options: Use Step Functions to orchestrate the preprocessing, training, and deployment sequence with retries
Use EventBridge rules alone to execute the full sequence of preprocessing, training, and deployment with retry handling
Use a single Lambda function with a 15-minute timeout to run the entire training workflow inline
Use CloudWatch alarms alone to chain preprocessing, training, and deployment tasks in strict order
q: A deployment workflow chains preprocessing, training, evaluation, and endpoint updates with retry logic. Which service orchestrates it?

explain: Bring Your Own Container lets teams package custom frameworks or system dependencies the built-in images lack. Built-in algorithms, inference recommenders, and jumpstart models cover standard cases instead.
options: Use a built-in SageMaker algorithm container that already includes the uncommon custom framework
Build a custom BYOC inference container that packages the rare framework with its dependencies
Use SageMaker JumpStart to deploy a foundation model that approximates the custom framework logic
Run the framework on a notebook instance and expose the notebook URL as the production endpoint
q: A team must serve a model built with a rare framework missing from SageMaker built-in images. What should it do?

explain: Endpoint autoscaling adds instances as traffic grows and removes them when it drops, holding latency steady. A fixed instance count either over-provisions or saturates during peaks.
options: Deploy a single large instance sized for the peak and keep it running through all off-peak hours
Switch the endpoint to Serverless Inference with unlimited concurrency and no scaling policies set
Enable endpoint autoscaling with a target-tracking policy on invocations per instance for traffic
Run batch transform every few minutes to approximate real-time scaling without a live endpoint
q: A real-time endpoint faces strong daily traffic swings but must keep latency stable. What is the best approach?

explain: Data capture logs request and response payloads to S3 for monitoring, bias, and drift analysis. Endpoint logs, training metrics, and pipeline lineage serve different observability purposes.
options: CloudWatch Logs from the training job that record loss curves and resource use during fitting
SageMaker Pipelines lineage tracking that links each dataset version to its training execution
Model Registry versioning that stores approval history and metadata for every candidate model
Endpoint data capture that logs live request and response payloads to S3 for later analysis
q: A team wants to analyze live production inputs later for drift and bias checks. Which feature should it enable?

explain: EventBridge reacts to events such as new S3 objects or registry approvals and can start pipelines or retraining. Step Functions executes the workflow itself rather than detecting the triggering event.
options: Configure an EventBridge rule that detects the new data event and starts the retraining workflow
Run a Step Functions execution on a fixed cron schedule that polls the S3 bucket every minute
Keep a Lambda function polling the registry approval API in a loop until the status changes
Enable endpoint autoscaling so that new data arrivals automatically trigger a full retraining run
q: Retraining should start automatically whenever new labeled data arrives in S3. Which service detects that event?

explain: Lambda has a 15-minute maximum execution time, so long training or batch jobs fail there. It suits lightweight glue such as preprocessing triggers, notifications, and deployment approvals.
options: Run the multi-hour model training job inside a single Lambda invocation with maximum memory across zones
Use Lambda for lightweight glue such as notifications, approvals, and triggering pipeline runs
Execute the full batch transform over terabytes of data inside one synchronous Lambda call
Host the large model artifact in Lambda layers and serve all production traffic from Lambda
q: What is an appropriate use of Lambda inside an ML deployment workflow?

explain: MWAA runs managed Apache Airflow, so teams with existing DAGs and operators can migrate them directly. Step Functions and Pipelines use different authoring models than Airflow DAGs.
options: Rewrite every Airflow DAG as a Step Functions state machine with Lambda functions for each task
Replace the Airflow scheduler with EventBridge rules that invoke each pipeline stage independently
Run the existing DAGs on MWAA, the managed Airflow service, with minimal rewriting of operators
Move all DAG logic into SageMaker training scripts and trigger them manually from the console
q: A team already orchestrates ML work with Apache Airflow DAGs on premises. Which AWS service migrates them most directly?

explain: Serverless Inference bills per invocation with scale-to-zero but adds cold starts, while provisioned real-time endpoints cost continuously but hold steady latency. The choice hinges on traffic steadiness and latency tolerance.
options: Serverless Inference always gives lower latency than provisioned endpoints under any traffic shape in every region
Provisioned endpoints bill per invocation while serverless endpoints bill per hour of uptime used
Both options scale identically, so cost and latency outcomes never differ between the two modes
Serverless scales to zero and bills per use with cold starts; provisioned costs continuously, stays warm
q: How do SageMaker Serverless Inference and provisioned real-time endpoints differ on cost versus latency?

explain: A 50 MB payload exceeds the real-time limit of 25 MB and the serverless limit of 4 MB, and 10-minute runs exceed the 60-second cap. Asynchronous inference supports payloads up to 1 GB and processing times up to one hour, so check these limits first.
options: Check payload size limits and timeout caps first, since large inputs rule out real-time and serverless
Compare only the hourly price of GPU versus CPU instances and pick the cheapest available type
Select the endpoint with the most provisioned concurrency regardless of input size constraints
Benchmark only average latency on tiny samples and assume results transfer to 50 MB payload sizes
q: A model accepts 50 MB video files with 10-minute inference times. What is the first selection criterion?

explain: Shadow variants receive a mirrored copy of live traffic while the current variant keeps serving responses. A/B testing splits traffic between variants, and blue/green shifts it in planned steps.
options: Run an A/B test that splits live traffic evenly and serves predictions from both model variants simultaneously
Deploy a shadow variant that mirrors live traffic for comparison while the current variant serves
Perform a blue/green deployment that shifts the full traffic weight to the new variant at once
Launch a batch transform job that replays last month of logs to approximate live serving behavior
q: A team wants to validate a new model on live traffic without affecting any user response. Which strategy fits?

explain: Canary and linear shifts move a small percentage first and roll back on alarm, while all-at-once blue/green exposes every user immediately. Gradual guardrails are the exam's expected safe pattern.
options: Update the endpoint all at once during peak traffic and monitor dashboards manually for regressions closely
Delete the production endpoint first, then recreate it with the new model to guarantee a clean state
Shift traffic gradually with canary or linear steps and roll back automatically on CloudWatch alarms
Deploy the new model to a notebook instance and redirect production DNS to the notebook endpoint URL
q: How should a team roll out a new model version to a production endpoint with minimal user impact?

explain: Multi-model endpoints suit many small models with similar serving stacks sharing containers, but GPU-heavy or framework-divergent models need isolation. Loading or memory contention breaks the shared-container assumption.
options: Hundreds of small scikit-learn models with identical containers and low per-model invocation rates each day
Dozens of regional variants of one model sharing the same framework and container dependencies
A catalog of rarely used lightweight models that tolerate on-demand loading latency on cache miss
Several large GPU models with conflicting frameworks that each need dedicated memory and containers
q: In which scenario is a SageMaker multi-model endpoint NOT a good fit?

explain: Inference pipelines chain preprocessing, prediction, and postprocessing containers behind one endpoint, avoiding extra hops. Separate endpoints, Lambda chains, or batch jobs add latency and complexity.
options: Use a SageMaker inference pipeline chaining preprocessing, prediction, and postprocessing containers
Deploy three separate real-time endpoints and call them sequentially from the client application code path
Chain Lambda functions between two endpoints to transform payloads with intermediate S3 staging
Run batch transform for preprocessing and a real-time endpoint only for the final prediction step
q: A deployment needs tokenization, model prediction, and business-rule postprocessing per request. What is the cleanest design?

explain: BYOC images must implement the SageMaker serving contract such as /ping and /invocations handlers. Framework choice alone does not make a custom image servable on an endpoint.
options: Sign the container image with a KMS key and store the model artifact in the same ECR repository
Implement the /ping and /invocations HTTP handlers so the endpoint can probe and invoke the server
Install the newest CUDA toolkit in the image so SageMaker automatically detects the custom framework
Copy the training script into the image because SageMaker reuses it directly as the serving entrypoint
q: What must a custom BYOC inference container implement to serve correctly on a SageMaker endpoint?

explain: A ProcessingStep runs scripts such as Spark or scikit-learn jobs, while TrainingStep fits models. Evaluation runs as a processing job whose metrics feed a ConditionStep. Registration only records an already trained artifact.
options: TrainingStep, because it launches the distributed fitting job over the prepared feature dataset
ConditionStep, because it calculates accuracy and F1 metrics that validate the prepared inputs
ProcessingStep, because it runs the Spark and scikit-learn scripts that build features at scale
RegisterModel, because it stores the final artifact together with its feature engineering lineage
q: A pipeline must run distributed Spark feature engineering before training. Which step performs that work?

explain: The ConditionStep branches on evaluation metrics, for example registering only when accuracy passes a threshold. Evaluation computes the numbers but does not branch the workflow.
options: Add a second TrainingStep that retrains with higher capacity whenever the accuracy metric drops low
Add a ProcessingStep that rewrites the evaluation script with stricter assertions on every run
Add a LambdaStep that deletes low-scoring model artifacts from S3 after each pipeline execution
Add a ConditionStep that registers the model only when the evaluation metric meets the threshold
q: A pipeline should register the model only if F1 exceeds 0.85. Which step implements that gate?

explain: Model Monitor baselines capture data statistics and constraints at training time for later comparison. Endpoint scaling policies, registry approvals, and data capture storage address other concerns.
options: Generate a Model Monitor baseline with data statistics and constraints during the training pipeline
Enable endpoint autoscaling with aggressive cooldowns and step policies so traffic spikes never distort metrics
Require Model Registry manual approval before any baseline statistics are computed or persisted
Turn on endpoint data capture with full payload sampling to replace the need for any baseline
q: A team wires drift detection into its training pipeline. What must the pipeline produce for production comparison?

explain: PendingManualApproval blocks deployment until a reviewer approves, creating the human gate. Approved releases it, while pipeline steps and endpoint policies do not enforce review gates.
options: Mark the version Approved immediately after training finishes so deployment proceeds without further review
Set the version to PendingManualApproval so deployment waits until a reviewer explicitly approves it
Delete the version from the registry and redeploy the previous artifact to simulate a review gate
Enable endpoint autoscaling with zero minimum instances so traffic pauses until reviewers respond
q: How does a team configure the Model Registry so no version reaches production without human review?

explain: SageMaker Projects standardize templates with staging and production accounts, approvals, and pipelines. A single shared notebook or manual console steps cannot enforce that separation.
options: Share one notebook instance where developers promote models by copying artifacts between folders
Trigger production retraining directly from developer notebooks whenever experiments look better
Use SageMaker Projects with separate staging and production environments plus approval gates
Run CodeBuild inside the development account and deploy straight to the production endpoint
q: A company needs separate staging and production environments with promotion approvals. Which setup delivers this?

explain: CodePipeline stages run CodeBuild for tests and require manual approval before production deployment. Direct notebook deployment skips testing, versioning, and the approval gate entirely.
options: Deploy each notebook checkpoint directly to the production endpoint to shorten the release cycle
Run unit tests locally on laptops and copy the model artifact to production with the S3 console
Let training jobs overwrite the production endpoint as soon as fitting finishes to save time
Gate production deployment in CodePipeline on CodeBuild tests plus a manual approval action
q: Where should model tests and the production approval gate live in an ML CI/CD design?

explain: Step Functions integrates with SageMaker jobs using run-a-job patterns that pause for completion and catch failures. Fire-and-forget Lambda invocations lose tracking of long-running executions.
options: Use Step Functions SageMaker integrations that wait for job completion and handle failures natively
Invoke each SageMaker job from Lambda with fire-and-forget calls and no callback or status check on completion
Poll training status from a notebook in a loop and update the endpoint manually when it finishes
Chain EventBridge rules directly to training jobs without any central state tracking or retries
q: A Step Functions workflow must launch training jobs and continue only after they complete. What is the right pattern?

explain: GPU instances cut latency for deep learning but cost far more per hour, while inference-optimized CPU or Inf1/Inf2 instances serve many models cheaply. Autoscaling and data capture do not change per-instance economics.
options: GPU instances always minimize total cost because faster inference completely eliminates all other charges
GPU instances lower latency at higher hourly cost; CPU or Inferentia instances cut cost per request
Instance type never affects latency or cost since SageMaker normalizes performance across families
Data capture sampling rates determine instance pricing more than the underlying hardware family
q: How should a team reason about GPU versus CPU or Inferentia instance types for an endpoint?

explain: Inference Recommender benchmarks instance types against latency and cost targets and recommends configurations. Manual guessing, registry approvals, and data capture do not rightsize endpoints.
options: Pick the largest GPU instance available to guarantee latency under every conceivable traffic spike
Copy the training instance type to the endpoint because training hardware always serves cheapest
Run SageMaker Inference Recommender to benchmark instance types against latency and cost goals
Enable full data capture sampling and infer the cheapest instance from the captured payload sizes
q: A team must rightsize endpoint instances against latency and cost targets. Which tool automates the comparison?

explain: Full 100 percent capture on high-traffic endpoints inflates S3 storage and processing costs, so sampling keeps monitoring affordable. Disabling capture entirely removes drift and bias visibility.
options: Disable data capture completely on all endpoints to eliminate the associated S3 storage charges
Capture every payload at 100 percent on high-traffic endpoints and retain the stored data indefinitely
Route capture data through provisioned GPU instances to compress payloads before S3 delivery
Use sampling rates and retention limits on data capture to bound S3 and processing costs carefully
q: Data capture costs are growing on a high-traffic endpoint. How can the team control them without losing monitoring?

explain: Async endpoints accept large payloads from S3 and return results to S3 with SNS notifications, tolerating hour-long runs. Real-time and serverless options cap payload size and duration far below these needs.
options: Use asynchronous inference with an S3 input location and SNS completion notifications for long jobs
Use a real-time endpoint with synchronous calls that wait up to an hour for each document result to return
Use Serverless Inference with maximum memory and concurrency to absorb the large document bursts
Use a multi-model endpoint that keeps every language model variant pinned in memory at all times
q: A transcription model processes 30-minute audio files submitted unpredictably. Which deployment fits?

explain: MaxConcurrentTransforms and instance count parallelize batch shards, while MultiRecord and batch strategy tune payload grouping. A single instance with default settings leaves throughput on the table.
options: Run the job on a single small instance with default settings and wait for the slow sequential pass to end
Tune MaxConcurrentTransforms, instance count, and payload batching to parallelize shards effectively
Replace the batch job with synchronous real-time invocations issued one row at a time from Lambda
Increase the endpoint autoscaling cooldown so batch shards accumulate before processing begins
q: A batch transform job over terabytes of data is too slow. Which tuning approach improves throughput?

explain: Parameter Store and Secrets Manager inject configuration and credentials at deployment time, keeping images portable. Baking secrets into images or hardcoding endpoints leaks credentials and blocks promotion.
options: Bake database passwords and endpoint URLs directly into the container image separately for each environment
Hardcode production credentials in the inference script so the container starts without lookups
Inject configuration and secrets via Parameter Store or Secrets Manager resolved at deployment time
Store secrets in the training data S3 bucket so both training and serving can read the same file
q: A BYOC container needs different database credentials in staging and production. How should it receive them?

explain: Async inference scales from zero, accepts large S3 payloads, and tolerates 15-minute cold starts, while provisioned concurrency on real-time endpoints would idle expensively. Serverless caps payload size and duration.
options: A provisioned real-time endpoint with high minimum instance counts to absorb the 15-minute backlog
A Serverless Inference endpoint with maximum concurrency handling each burst synchronously in memory
A multi-model endpoint that preloads all document models and keeps instances warm around the clock
An asynchronous endpoint that scales from zero, accepts S3 payloads, and tolerates cold starts well
q: Document batches arrive in 15-minute bursts with large payloads, then nothing for hours. Which design minimizes cost while meeting SLAs?

explain: SageMaker Model Registry with cross-account resource policies plus CodePipeline promotion stages enforces review gates per environment. Copying artifacts manually between buckets bypasses approvals and lineage.
options: Promote versions through the Model Registry with cross-account policies and gated pipeline stages
Copy model.tar.gz files between account buckets manually and update each endpoint from the console
Share a single endpoint across accounts with open IAM access so every team deploys without gates
Retrain independently in each account from raw data and skip registry versioning to save approval time
q: A regulated enterprise promotes models across dev, staging, and prod accounts with review gates. Which pattern satisfies auditors?

explain: Multi-record batch with MiniBatch splits large S3 inputs into shards processed in parallel, unlike single-record synchronous serving. Autoscaling a real-time endpoint cannot match offline bulk economics.
options: Serve each record synchronously from a real-time endpoint with provisioned concurrency for the peak
Configure batch transform with multi-record batches and S3 sharding to parallelize offline scoring
Stream records through Serverless Inference one by one with maximum memory per invocation set
Queue records in an async endpoint with per-record SNS notifications and sequential processing
q: A genomics workload scores 100 GB of S3 sequences nightly with no interactive latency need. Which configuration maximizes throughput per dollar?

explain: Endpoint invocation metrics with low invocation counts but high latency point to cold loading on a multi-model endpoint. Throttling errors or capture growth would implicate different limits.
options: CloudWatch throttling errors on Serverless Inference indicate that provisioned concurrency is exhausted
Rising S3 storage from data capture indicates that payload sampling rates are set far too aggressively
P99 latency spikes with low invocation counts indicate cold model loading on a multi-model endpoint
Training job CPU metrics showing saturation indicate that the endpoint instance type is undersized
q: P99 latency spikes on a multi-model endpoint while overall invocations stay low. What is the most likely cause?

explain: A CallbackStep sends a message with a token to an external process and waits for the response, so the pipeline can pause for a human decision. A LambdaStep runs a function and returns, so it cannot wait for sign-off. Approving in the Model Registry with an EventBridge rule is the other valid pattern. Automatic registration or deletion removes the governance gate.
options: Register every trained model automatically and deploy it straight to the production endpoint stage
Delete the Model Registry from the flow and copy artifacts to production with S3 replication rules
Add a TrainingStep that retrains continuously until metrics pass, without any human decision point
Add a CallbackStep that sends a token to the approver and waits for the response before registration
q: A pipeline must pause for compliance sign-off between evaluation and registration. How should this be implemented?

explain: Warm pools keep training clusters ready and provisioned concurrency on a serverless endpoint keeps inference capacity warm, cutting queueing on both sides. Spot instances and scale-to-zero add startup delay at exactly the wrong moment.
options: Use SageMaker Training warm pools plus provisioned concurrency on a serverless endpoint to cut startup delays
Use Spot instances for training and scale-to-zero serverless inference to minimize hourly charges
Run training on single small instances and serve from one shared notebook to reduce idle capacity
Disable all caching and concurrency so every request provisions fresh capacity with full isolation
q: A flash-sale recommender must retrain hourly and serve traffic spikes instantly. Which combination meets both latency goals?

explain: MWAA workers with SageMaker operators submit training jobs and sensors wait for completion, fitting Airflow semantics. Workers lack GPUs for fitting, and runtime installs alone do not orchestrate jobs.
options: Run model fitting directly on MWAA workers with heavy dependencies installed on the schedulers
Use Airflow SageMaker operators to submit training jobs and sensors to wait for their completion
Install the SageMaker SDK on workers and invoke endpoints synchronously inside short task loops
Replace Airflow sensors with fixed sleep timers that assume training always finishes in one hour
q: An Airflow DAG on MWAA must trigger SageMaker training and wait before downstream tasks. What is the correct pattern?

explain: Model cards document intended use, metrics, and limitations, and registry lineage links versions to data and jobs. Autoscaling policies and capture sampling describe operations, not model transparency.
options: Endpoint autoscaling policies that record how instance counts reacted to past traffic spike events
Data capture sampling configurations that log the percentage of payloads retained for monitoring
Model cards with intended use and metrics plus registry lineage linking versions to data and jobs
CodeBuild logs from the CI pipeline that show test durations and build container image versions
q: Auditors demand traceability from each production model version back to its data, metrics, and intended use. What provides this?

explain: Provisioned real-time inference plus auto rollback on alarms protects the strict sub-100 ms SLA, which serverless cold starts and async queues cannot meet. Batch precompute cannot cover unseen live inputs.
options: Serverless Inference with scale-to-zero and per-invocation billing to minimize cost during off-peak
Asynchronous inference with S3 outputs and SNS notifications to absorb unpredictable request bursts
Nightly batch transform that precomputes scores for known users and caches them for live lookup
Provisioned real-time inference with autoscaling plus automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarms
q: A video platform needs sub-100 ms personalization for volatile live traffic with safe rollouts. Which architecture fits?

explain: ECR image scanning plus signed images, endpoint IAM roles, and KMS encryption cover supply chain and data protection together. Public images and open invocation skip both controls.
options: Scan and sign BYOC images in ECR, restrict invocation with IAM roles, and encrypt artifacts with KMS
Pull public images at deploy time and allow open endpoint invocation to simplify cross-team access
Embed AWS credentials in the image layers so tasks authenticate without assuming any IAM role
Disable encryption on artifacts and logs to reduce latency overhead on the inference code path
q: A healthcare deployment uses BYOC with PHI payloads. Which combination addresses supply-chain and data protection?
A client sends 8 MB JSON payloads to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. Inference takes 90 seconds per request and callers can wait for a notification. Which option should the team use?
options: Split each payload into 1 MB chunks and call the real-time endpoint in a tight retry loop
Move to Serverless Inference with maximum memory and poll the endpoint synchronously
Use asynchronous inference with an S3 input, SQS queueing, and SNS completion alerts
Keep the real-time endpoint and raise the timeout to 15 minutes with larger instances
explain: The 8 MB payloads fit the real-time limit of 25 MB, but 90-second requests exceed the 60-second real-time timeout. Asynchronous inference accepts up to 1 GB and one hour of processing, with queueing and SNS notifications.

q: A prototype classifier receives about 100 requests per day at random hours. Each call runs in 3 seconds with a 2 MB payload, and cold starts are acceptable. Which is the cheapest deployment?
options: A provisioned real-time endpoint on ml.m5.xlarge kept running all day and night
A Serverless Inference endpoint that scales to zero and bills per invocation
An asynchronous endpoint with provisioned throughput reserved around the clock
A batch transform cluster left running to poll for new requests continuously
explain: Sporadic short inferences with small payloads fit Serverless Inference, which scales to zero and bills per use. A provisioned endpoint would idle most of the day while async and batch add unneeded delay.

q: A media firm submits 600 MB video files at burst times. Each job runs 8 minutes, and the app polls a result location after a push alert. Which pattern fits?
options: Asynchronous inference with S3 input and output paths plus SNS completion notification
Real-time inference with synchronous calls held open for the full 8 minutes
Serverless Inference with 4 MB inline payloads sent in parallel batches
Batch transform with a persistent endpoint kept warm for interactive polling
explain: Large payloads with minute-scale runtimes and notification needs match async inference: S3-based I/O, internal queueing, scale to zero, and SNS alerts. Real-time and serverless caps block this shape.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: A bank must score 5 TB of archived transactions in S3 every Sunday night. No user waits for a live reply. Which approach is simplest and cheapest?
options: A real-time endpoint with autoscaling left running all weekend for live queries
An asynchronous endpoint invoked millions of times with one SNS alert per row
A serverless endpoint called in a loop with maximum concurrency all night
A batch transform job over the S3 prefix with S3 output and no live endpoint
explain: Scheduled offline scoring of terabytes in S3 is the batch transform use case: no persistent endpoint, parallel shards, S3 in and S3 out. Live endpoint styles add idle cost and per-request overhead.

q: A retailer hosts 300 small per-store models on the same scikit-learn container. Each model is called a few times daily. How can it cut endpoint cost?
options: Deploy 300 dedicated real-time endpoints, one per store, with reserved capacity
Use one multi-model endpoint sharing containers and select models via TargetModel
Run a nightly batch job that precomputes every possible input for every store
Deploy 300 serverless endpoints with maximum memory and fixed concurrency
explain: A multi-model endpoint hosts many models with one serving stack and loads them on demand via the TargetModel parameter. It suits many same-framework, rarely invoked models far better than one endpoint each.

q: A team must serve an XGBoost model and a PyTorch model from one endpoint, each with its own container, and call each directly. Which option supports this?
options: A multi-model endpoint that forces all models to share one identical container
A Serverless Inference endpoint that merges both frameworks into one runtime
A multi-container endpoint with direct invocation routing to each container
A batch transform job that fuses both containers into a single offline run
explain: Multi-container endpoints run distinct containers behind one endpoint and support direct invocation of a chosen container. Multi-model endpoints instead require a shared serving stack across models.
source: Adattata da Udemy – practice test MLA-C01

q: Company policy says no model may reach production until a lead marks its registry entry as accepted. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: Register each version as a ModelPackage and require ApprovalStatus Approved before deploy
Copy model.tar.gz between S3 prefixes and overwrite the endpoint config manually
Enable endpoint autoscaling so traffic only flows after a manual instance start
Run training with Spot instances so interrupted jobs never reach production
explain: The Model Registry versions ModelPackages with approval states such as PendingManualApproval and Approved. CI/CD then deploys only versions marked Approved, creating the required human gate.

q: An ML workflow needs Lambda preprocessing, a SageMaker training job, a metric check, and an SNS approval pause with visual tracking. Which service fits best?
options: A single Lambda function that runs training, evaluation, and approval inline
An EventBridge rule alone that executes training code and waits for approval
A SageMaker training job that embeds the approval dialog in its entrypoint
A Step Functions state machine chaining jobs with Choice states and callbacks
explain: Step Functions orchestrates Lambda, SageMaker jobs, Choice branches, retries, and human-approval callbacks with visual execution tracking. Lambda alone cannot run long jobs and EventBridge only routes events.

q: A team must shift 10% of live traffic to a new model, watch error alarms, then proceed linearly. Which deployment setup enables this?
options: A real-time EndpointConfig with production variants, canary shift, and alarm rollback
An async endpoint with two queues drained at fixed rates without metrics
A batch transform job replaying last week logs against both model versions
A serverless endpoint redeployed in place with full traffic cutover at once
